Rashi on Ketubot 33b:10:1.english: To one who slaughters by means of another - The thief instructed his agent to slaughter [it].

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:11:1.hebrew: וכי - שליח חוטא, ושולח מתחייב קנס דארבעה וחמשה? והא קיימא לן בקדושין (מב:), אין שליח לדבר עבירה: מכירה אי אפשר אלא ע"י אחר, שהלוקח לוקחו ממנו:
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:11:1.english: And does - [the] agent sin and [the] sender become liable for the penalty of fourfold and fivefold [payment]? Yet we have an established principle in Kiddushin (42b): there is no agent for a matter of transgression. A sale is impossible except through another, as the buyer purchases it from him.

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:12:1.english: For [tachat] the ox - [Scripture] could have written, "he shall pay beshor" [for an ox, using the prefix be- instead of tachat].

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:13:1.english: [If] he performs [it] himself, he is not liable - For he is put to death.

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:13:2.hebrew: לאו משום דלא מיחייב הוא - דחיובא רמיא עליה, אלא משום דקם ליה בדרבה מיניה:
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:13:2.english: It is not because he is not liable - for liability rests upon him; rather, [he is exempt] because he incurs the greater [punishment] than it.

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:1:2.hebrew: ולא שני לך כו' - יסורי המלכות הכאה שאין לה קצבה היא, אבל מלקות יש לה קצבה, ארבעים:
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:1:2.english: And is there no difference to you, etc. - The tortures of the monarchy are a beating that has no limit, whereas lashes have a limit [of] forty.

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:2:1.hebrew: הניחא לרבנן דאמרי - בסנהדרין באלו הן הנשרפים (עט.), נתכוון להרוג את זה והרג את זה — חייב, והאי ונתת נפש ממש קאמר. אית לן למידק ואוקמי קרא בשהתרו בו, ולמילף דאע"ג דאיכא התראה, יענש ממון כשאין שם מיתה:
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:2:1.english: This works out well according to the Rabbis, who say - [As taught] in Sanhedrin, in [the chapter] Eilu Hen HaNisrafin (79a): [If] one intended to kill this [person] and killed that [person], he is liable [for execution], and this [verse], "And you shall give [a life for a life]," refers to an actual life. [Therefore,] we must infer precisely and establish the verse as [referring to a case] where they warned him, and learn that even though there is a warning, he is punished with monetary [payment] when there is no death [penalty] there.

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:2:2.hebrew: אלא לרבי דאמר - התם, נתכוון להרוג את זה והרג את זה אינו נהרג, אלא משלם דמי האשה ליורשיה. אם כן, אפשר לאוקמי קרא בשלא התרו בו, ומשום הכי: כי אין אסון — משלם דמי ולדות, וכי יש אסון — משלם דמי אשה; אבל אתרו ביה — אימא לך לוקה ואינו משלם:
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:2:2.english: However, according to Rabbi, who said - There, [if] one intended to kill this [person] and killed that [person], he is not executed, rather he pays the value of the woman to her heirs. If so, it is possible to establish the verse as [referring to a case] where they did not forewarn him, and because of this: when there is no fatality, he pays the value of the offspring, and when there is a fatality, he pays the value of the woman; however, [if] they forewarned him, I could say to you [that] he receives lashes and does not pay.

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:2:3.hebrew: מאי איכא למימר - מהיכא תיתי חובל בחבירו לתשלומין, ואף כשהתרו בו:
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:2:3.english: What can be said - From where would we derive [that] one who injures his fellow [is liable] for monetary payment, even when they forewarned him?

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:3:1.hebrew: על משענתו - כדמתרגמינן על בוריו, ששב לכחו ולאיתנו הראשון:
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:3:1.english: With his staff - As we translate [in the Targum]: al buryeh [upon his full health], [meaning] that he has returned to his strength and his original vigor.

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:3:2.hebrew: אלא מלמד שחובשין אותו - לא נאמר מקרא זה אלא ללמדך, דהיכא דהכהו ולא מת ונפל למשכב, יחבשו את המכה ההוא בבית האסורין עד שנראה: אם "יקום והתהלך בחוץ" — אז "ונקה המכה"; מכלל דעד השתא לא יצא מידי בית דין, אלא נחבש:
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:3:2.english: Rather, [it] teaches that one imprisons him - This verse was stated only to teach you that where [one] struck him and he did not die, but fell bedridden, they imprison that assailant in prison until we see: if "he rises and walks outside," then "he who struck him is absolved" — which implies that until now he had not been released from the court, but rather was imprisoned.

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:3:3.hebrew: ואי מיית קטלינן ליה - [כיון דאמרת חובשין, מכלל דאי מיית ניזק, קטלינן ליה להאי; דאי לאו לקטלא, למאי חבשינן ליה:
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:3:3.english: And if he dies, we kill him - Since you said [that] we imprison [him], it follows by implication that if the injured party dies, we execute this [assailant]; for if [it were] not for execution, why would we imprison him?

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:4:2.english: For the lesser matter - Lashes for [violating] "he shall not add," when he wounds [him] and he does not die.

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:4:3.hebrew: ואמר רחמנא - להיכא דלא מת, דאיכא ממון ומלקות, נידון בממון, דכתיב "שבתו יתן":
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:4:3.english: And the Merciful One states - [Referring] to a case where [the victim] did not die, where there is [liability for both] monetary payment and lashes, he is judged with monetary payment, as it is written: “His loss of livelihood he shall give.”

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:5:1.hebrew: ממאי - דהאי ״והכה איש את רעהו״ במזיד קא משתעי, והאי ״ונקה״ — דילפינן מיניה חבישה — ״ונקה״ מקטלא קאמר, דתשמע מינה דאי מיית קטלינן ליה, ועל כרחין בהתרו בו:
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:5:1.english: From where - [do we know] that this [verse], "and a man strikes his fellow," speaks of an intentional [act], and [that] this [word], "and he shall be acquitted" — from which we derive imprisonment — means "acquitted" from execution, so that you infer from it that if he dies, we execute him, and perforce [it is] where they forewarned him?

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:7:1.hebrew: דלמא בשוגג - משתעי, ולא התרו בו, וחבישה לאו לקטלא, ונקה נמי לאו לקטלא אלא מגלות דערי מקלט; וחבישה דילפינן מינה, לגלות קאמר. ומשום הכי, כי נקה מגלות, ישלם ממון, אבל היכא דאתרו ביה, אימא לך דכי לא מיית, לוקה ואינו משלם:
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:7:1.english: Perhaps [it was] unwittingly - [The verse] is speaking [of an unwitting offender], and they did not warn him, and the imprisonment is not for execution, and "he shall be absolved" is also not [absolved] from execution, rather from exile to the cities of refuge; and the imprisonment that we derive from it refers to exile. And because of this, when he is absolved from exile, he pays money; but where they warned him, I would say to you that when [the victim] does not die, [the assailant] is flogged and does not pay.

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:8:1.hebrew: ריש לקיש מהדר אשינויא דרומיא דרמינן בריש שמעתין, <abbr title="מתניתין">מתני'</abbr> דמכות אדכתובות:
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:8:1.english: Reish Lakish is returning to the resolution of the contradiction that we raised at the beginning of our discussion, [contrasting] the Mishnah of Makkot with [that] of Ketubot:

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:8:2.hebrew: הא מני - מתניתין דקתני בא על אחותו נותן קנס, ר"מ היא, דאמר לעיל: לוקה ומשלם, שלא השם מביאו לידי מכות מביאו לידי תשלומין:
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:8:2.english: Whose [opinion] is this - Our Mishnah, which teaches [that] one who has intercourse with his sister pays a fine, is [the opinion of] Rabbi Meir, who said earlier: One is flogged and pays, for it is not the [same] category that brings him to lashes [that] brings him to payment.

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:8:3.hebrew: אפי' בתו נמי - דמיקטיל עלה, לישלם! דהא לא סבירא ליה לר"מ דפטור משום דרבה מיניה. ואמאי תנן מתני': "הבא על בתו פטור מן הקנס":
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:8:3.english: Even his daughter too - on account of whom he is executed, he should pay! For Rabbi Meir does not hold that he is exempt because of [the punishment] that is greater than it. Why, then, did our Mishnah teach: "One who cohabits with his daughter is exempt from the fine"?

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:9:1.hebrew: וטבח בשבת - איכא חיוב מיתה, וכן לעבודת כוכבים:
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:9:1.english: And slaughtered [it] on Shabbat - There is liability for the death penalty, and likewise for idolatry.

Rashi on Ketubot 33b:9:2.hebrew: שור הנסקל - לקמן פריך, הא לא שוה מידי:
Rashi on Ketubot 33b:9:2.english: An ox that [was sentenced to be] stoned - Later [the Gemara] asks: Behold, it is not worth anything.

Tosafot on Ketubot 33b:13:1.hebrew: לאו משום דלא מיחייב כו' - אע"ג דהכא אפי' לצאת ידי שמים אינו חייב — דדוקא בממון הוא דאמר רבא בהשוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ צא. ושם): "אתנן אסרה תורה אפי' בא על אמו", דמיחייב בבא לצאת ידי שמים, אבל קנס לא מיחייב אלא ע"פ ב"ד, כדאמרי': "אשר ירשיעון אלהים" — פרט למרשיע עצמו — מ"מ ניחא; דכיון שהיה ראוי להתחייב אם לא היה מתחייב בנפשו, מתחייב נמי אממון ע"י שליח, כיון שאינו מתחייב בנפשו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 33b:13:1.english: "Not due to [the fact] that he is not liable, etc." - Even though here [in the case of a fine] he is not liable even to fulfill his obligation toward Heaven — for it is specifically with regard to monetary [obligations] that Rava says in [the chapter] HaSokher Et HaPoalim (Bava Metzia 91a and there): "The Torah forbade a [harlot's] hire even if he cohabited with his mother," [meaning] that he is liable when he comes to fulfill his obligation toward Heaven, whereas [for] a fine one is not liable except by [a ruling of] a court, as we say: "Whom the judges shall condemn" — excluding one who condemns himself — nevertheless, [the answer] is satisfactory; for since he would have been fit to become liable if he had not been liable for his life, he also becomes liable for the monetary [payment] through an agent, since [then] he is not liable for his life:

Tosafot on Ketubot 33b:1:1.hebrew: ודלמא מלקות חמור - הוה מצי לשנויי: מסתברא מיתה חמורה, שכן ניתנה לאנשי עיר הנידחת, כדאמרי' בפ"ד מיתות (סנהדרין נ.):
Tosafot on Ketubot 33b:1:1.english: And perhaps lashes are more severe - [The Gemara] could have answered: It is reasonable [that] death is more severe, since it was given to the inhabitants of an idolatrous city, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 50a):

Tosafot on Ketubot 33b:1:2.hebrew: אילמלי נגדוה לחנניה מישאל ועזריה הוו פלחי לצלמא - תימה: מנא לן? דהא אמרי' בהרואה (ברכות סא:): כשהוציאו את ר"ע, אמר: "כל ימי הייתי מצטער על פסוק זה, אימתי יבא לידי ואקיימנו 'בכל נפשך'". אלמא משמע ד"בכל נפשך" מיירי אפי' היו מייסרין את האדם ביסורין קשין דומיא דר' עקיבא, שהיו מסרקין בשרו במסרקי ברזל, וכ"ש לנגודי! ואור"ת דאותו צלם לא היה עבודת כוכבים ממש, אלא היה עשוי לכבוד המלך, ואעפ"כ היה בו קידוש השם, ולכך מסרו עצמן למיתה. והיינו דכתיב (דניאל ג): "לאלהך לית אנן פלחין ולצלם דהבא די אקימת לא נסגוד" — משמע שהצלם לא היה תופס באלהות. ומיהו "פלחו לצלמא" משמע שהצלם היה עבודת כוכבים, מדקאמר "פלחו":
Tosafot on Ketubot 33b:1:2.english: "Had they flogged Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, they would have worshipped the image" - This is astonishing: from where do we know [this]? For we say in [the chapter entitled] HaRo'eh (Berakhot 61b): When they took Rabbi Akiva out [to be executed], he said: "All my days I was distressed over this verse — when will it come into my hand so that I may fulfill it: 'with all your soul'?" Thus it implies that "with all your soul" refers even [to a case where] they were afflicting a person with harsh tortures like Rabbi Akiva, whose flesh they were combing with iron combs — and all the more so to flogging! And Rabbeinu Tam says that that image was not actual idolatry, rather it was made for the honor of the king; and even so, there was sanctification of God's Name involved, and therefore they surrendered themselves to death. And this is what is written (Daniel 3): "Your god we do not worship, and to the golden image that you set up we will not bow down" — implying that the image was not considered a deity. However, [the Gemara's wording] "they would have worshipped (pelachu) the image" implies that the image was idolatry, since it says "pelachu" [worshipped].

Tosafot on Ketubot 33b:7:1.hebrew: דלמא בשוגג ונקה מגלות - תימה לר"י: היכי שייך גלות אם מת אחר שחבשוהו ב' או שלשה ימים? הא אמרינן במי שאחזו (גיטין ע: ושם): שחט בו שנים או רוב שנים — הרי זה אינו גולה, דחיישינן שמא הרוח בלבלתו; וטעמא דגבי גלות אשכחן מילי טובא דפטור, כגון דרך עלייה, דגבי מיתה אין חילוק בין דרך עלייה לדרך ירידה — הכי נמי גבי גלות בעינן שימות מיד, כדכתיב: "ויפל עליו וימות", משמע מיד, ואע"ג דגבי מיתה נמי כתיב "מכה איש ומת". וי"ל דמשכחת לה בביתא דשישא, דלא חיישינן שמא הרוח בלבלתו, כדאמרינן התם. אי נמי: דוקא בשחט בו רוב שנים חיישינן שמא הרוח בלבלתו, דבקל הרוח מבלבלו; אבל בשאר חבלות אין הרוח מזיק כל כך, שיכולין לשמור יפה מבלבול רוח, לכרוך על המכה שום דבר. וא"ת: היכי מיתוקם קרא בשוגג? הא כתיב שבת בקרא: "רק שבתו יתן וגו'", ובשוגג לא מיחייב, כדאמרינן בס"פ כיצד הרגל (ב"ק כו: ושם) דמרבה מ"פצע תחת פצע" לחייב על השוגג כמזיד נזק, אבל לא ד' דברים! וי"ל דמשכחת לה בהוסיף לו רצועה אחת, דאמר בהמניח (שם לב:) דגולה, ואם לא מת חייב בד' דברים, ולא דמי לשאר שוגג. או כגון שנכנס לחנותו של נגר (שלא) ברשות, דמוכח התם לרב פפא דשייך ביה גלות וד' דברים. או נפל מן הגג ברוח מצויה, דחייב בד' דברים, כדאמרי' בסוף כיצד הרגל (שם כז.), ומסתברא דאם מת דגולה. ועוד, דאפשר דהוי שוגג על המיתה ומזיד על החבלה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 33b:7:1.english: "Perhaps [it is] unwittingly, and 'he shall be absolved' [means] of exile" - The R"I wonders: How is exile applicable if [the victim] died after they imprisoned [the assailant] for two or three days? Do we not say in [the chapter] Mi She'achazo (Gittin 70b and there): If one slaughtered both [pipes] or the majority of both, he is not exiled, because we are concerned lest the wind aggravated his [condition]? And the reason is that regarding exile we find many things where he is exempt — such as [killing] by way of ascending, whereas regarding the death penalty there is no distinction between by way of ascending and by way of descending — so too regarding exile, we require that he die immediately, as it is written: "and it fell upon him, and he died," which implies immediately, even though regarding the death penalty it is also written: "He who strikes a man so that he dies." And one can answer that you find [such a case] in a marble room, where we are not concerned lest the wind aggravated his [condition], as we say there. Alternatively: Specifically when he slaughtered the majority of both [pipes] are we concerned lest the wind aggravated his [condition], for the wind easily aggravates it; however, in other injuries the wind does not harm so much, for they can guard well against the aggravation of the wind by wrapping something over the wound. And if you ask: How can the verse be established [as referring to one who acted] unwittingly? Surely "loss of livelihood" is written in the verse: "only he shall pay for his loss of livelihood, etc.," and for an unwitting act one is not liable [for that], as we say at the end of the chapter Keitzad HaRegel (Bava Kamma 26b and there), where [the Gemara] derives from "wound for wound" to make one liable for an unwitting act just as for an intentional act for depreciation, but not for the [other] four payments! And one can answer that you find it where [the court officer] added one lash to him, regarding which [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] HaMeniach (ibid. 32b) that he is exiled, and if [the victim] did not die he is liable for the four payments, and it is not comparable to other unwitting acts. Or, for example, where one entered a carpenter's shop (without) permission, where it is proven there according to Rav Pappa that exile and the four payments are applicable to him. Or where one fell from the roof in a normal wind, where he is liable for the four payments, as we say at the end of Keitzad HaRegel (ibid. 27a), and it stands to reason that if [the victim] died, he is exiled. And furthermore, it is possible that he was unwitting regarding the death and intentional regarding the injury:

Tosafot on Ketubot 33b:9:1.hebrew: גנב שור הנסקל וטבחו משלם תשלומי ד' וה' - תימה, דתיקשי מהכא לריש לקיש, דאמר בפ' מרובה (בבא קמא עז: ושם): "כל היכא דליתיה במכירה, ליתיה בטביחה", והכא שור הנסקל ליתיה במכירה! וי"ל, דהתם קדשים חמירי דליתנהו כלל במכירה; אבל שור הנסקל, אם ימכרנו לעובד כוכבים — אין תופס דמיו. ולר"ת, שאומר דאין שור הנסקל נאסר מחיים — ניחא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 33b:9:1.english: [If one] stole an ox that was sentenced to be stoned and slaughtered it, he pays a payment of four or five [times the principal] - It is astonishing, for this should pose a difficulty for Reish Lakish, who said in the chapter [entitled] Merubeh (Bava Kamma 77b and elsewhere): "Wherever it is not [subject to] sale, it is not [subject to] slaughter," yet here an ox sentenced to be stoned is not [subject to] sale! And one can answer that there, consecrated [animals] are more stringent, for they are not [subject to] sale at all; whereas [with] an ox sentenced to be stoned, if one sells it to an idolater, it does not transfer [its prohibition to] its proceeds. And according to Rabbeinu Tam, who says that an ox sentenced to be stoned is not prohibited [from benefit] while alive, it is straightforward.
